envelope_schema.title: Presentation envelope
envelope_schema.description: Every resolved component payload has this one shape (Contract - Presentation Primitive, "The envelope"). `component` is closed to the members this catalogue release ships (line_chart, bar_chart, table, stat_card, note_narration, source_card); a member added later is a new catalogue release, per "The union is closed per release".

schema_version.description: the integer version of the catalogue schema this payload was generated against

component_id.description: globally unique, minted at creation; the id every edit tool targets

revision.description: increments on every applied edit; revisions are immutable once minted

else.$comment: Every member but note_narration resolves a frame, so provenance.inputs names at least the one frame it resolved; note_narration carries no frame_ref and its own inputs stays empty, the base bound (minItems 0) the $defs/provenance schema declares.

catalog_version.$comment: Calver, provisional; redefined in place pre-freeze rather than bumped, until a first real freeze fixes it.

spec_id.$comment: spec_ (Datasets) or ops_ (Analysis Toolkit) prefix per "Frame and series references"; hex-length bound is loose because the contract itself calls identifier spellings illustrative pending the identifier decision.

content_version.$comment: cv_ (Datasets) or ocv_ (Analysis Toolkit) prefix per "Frame and series references", matching the prefixes `spec_id` accepts; hex-length bound is loose for the same reason.

inputs.description: empty for a component with no frame_ref (note_narration); every other member names at least the one frame it resolved.

execution_ref.description: content-addressed identity of the Analysis Toolkit execution behind derived values; null for a direct read

ref.description: the Data Commons provenance dcid this entry was built from (for example `provenance/OECDCreditorReportingSystem` or `dc/base/WorldDevelopmentIndicators`), so a renderer can look the source up in the graph; absent on components minted before platforms wrote it

source.description: the Data Commons Source node behind the provenance (for a UN System Data Commons series, the agency provenance itself); absent on dataset versions minted before the origin catalogue

data_commons.description: the Data Commons the provenance is served from; absent on dataset versions minted before the origin catalogue

data_through.$comment: nullable: the upstream frame may not yet supply a coverage-through period.

next_expected.$comment: nullable: not every source publishes a refresh cadence.

kind.$comment: Closed vocabulary drawn from the contract's own examples ("provisional status, estimates, imputations, coverage gaps, comparability breaks"); the taxonomy is seam-owed to the Datasets/Analysis layers that populate it.

generated_at.description: the payload's generation timestamp, stamped by the assembler

citation.description: ready-to-paste string the assembler generates from the structured provenance fields

refreshed_from.description: the revision (of this same component_id) this payload was drawn from on newer data: the revision a render redrew without minting a new one, or the revision a refresh revision was minted from; null otherwise

line_chart.title: line_chart component
line_chart.description: Resolved payload for the `line_chart` catalogue member (Contract, "Worked component: the line chart").

authorship.$comment: Only "model" exists at launch (Contract's Model-authored-claims row); the enum stays closed rather than open-string so a future first-party/user authorship arrives as a deliberate catalogue change.

unit.$comment: Pass-through unit slot: null, an opaque graph-ref string, or a structured object. No conversion happens in Presentation; the structured object's own field set is seam-owed to the upstream unit design.

status.$comment: The status vocabulary the contract reserves: a derived-missing point (no observation for a visible series over the window/grain) and the source-supplied statuses that pass through unchanged.

id.description: derived by the assembler from the series' coordinates; the same selection always yields the same id

stat_card.title: stat_card component
stat_card.description: Resolved payload for the `stat_card` catalogue member: one headline number with label, unit, and an optional derived change (Contract, "The catalogue").

authorship.$comment: Only "model" exists at launch (Contract's Model-authored-claims row); the enum stays closed rather than open-string so a future first-party/user authorship arrives as a deliberate catalogue change.

period.description: The period the headline `value` covers: the observation's period, or the span a value derived from several periods covers.

unit.$comment: Pass-through unit slot, identical shape to line_chart's; no conversion happens in Presentation.

change.$comment: Optional: a headline with no requested comparison period carries no change. When present, both fields are mandatory -- a change with no stated derivation or basis is exactly the ambiguity stat_change_basis_observed exists to prevent.

derivation.$comment: Closed, golden-tested derivation set (Contract: "drawn from a closed, golden-tested derivation set: difference and percent change").

observed_period.$comment: A point at year, month or day grain, or a closed span `start/end` whose two ends share one grain. The frame grammar's period rule also requires start before end, which a pattern cannot compare.

bar_chart.title: bar_chart component
bar_chart.description: Resolved payload for the `bar_chart` catalogue member. Bars compare entities or periods, never both: entity mode bars one point per selected entity at one shared period or one shared span; period mode bars one series' points across a window, the same shape as `line_chart`.

category_axis.description: Entity mode names the dimension bars categorize by and the one shared period every bar was minted at. Period mode names the window bars span, the same shape line_chart's x_axis carries.

value_axis.description: The axis values are drawn on, whichever side orientation puts it.

then.$comment: Period mode bars one series across a window, so each bar's period is a point; only entity mode carries a span.

observed_period.$comment: A point at year, month or day grain, or a closed span `start/end` whose two ends share one grain. The frame grammar's period rule also requires start before end, which a pattern cannot compare.

unit.$comment: Pass-through unit slot: null, an opaque graph-ref string, or a structured object. No conversion happens in Presentation; the structured object's own field set is seam-owed to the upstream unit design.

status.$comment: The status vocabulary the contract reserves: a derived-missing point (no observation for a visible series over the window/grain) and the source-supplied statuses that pass through unchanged.

id.description: derived by the assembler from the series' coordinates; the same selection always yields the same id

table.title: table component
table.description: Resolved payload for the `table` catalogue member: one row per (selected coordinate, period), the cross-product of every arrayed selection.

columns.description: One entry per selected dimension, in select order, followed by period and value.

observed_period.$comment: A point at year, month or day grain, or a closed span `start/end` whose two ends share one grain. The frame grammar's period rule also requires start before end, which a pattern cannot compare.

unit.$comment: Pass-through unit slot: null, an opaque graph-ref string, or a structured object. No conversion happens in Presentation; the structured object's own field set is seam-owed to the upstream unit design.

series_id.description: the series identity the row belongs to, equal to the id a bar or line series would carry for the same coordinates

note_narration.title: note_narration component
note_narration.description: Resolved payload for the `note_narration` catalogue member: model-authored text, labelled as model voice.

authorship.$comment: Only "model" exists at launch, the same closed vocabulary the other components' title.authorship carries.

source_card.title: source_card component
source_card.description: Resolved payload for the `source_card` catalogue member: which of the envelope's own provenance.sources this card presents. Carries no duplicated source objects; provenance stays the single source of truth and this component is the presentation instruction.

line_chart.description: One line per selected series, over time.

select.description: Dimension name to value. At most one dimension may be an array of up to 8 values; the rest are single strings.

anyOf.description: The scale of the value axis. "log" plots the axis logarithmically and requires every visible series value to be positive. Absent means linear.
Fixed bounds for the value axis. Both keys are required when `range` is present, and a null bound follows the data. The fixed range must contain the visible data.

frame_ref.description: The pinned frame this component draws from, exactly as the data layer returned it.

relative_period.description: A period counted from the latest one: `anchor` "latest" is the newest period at least half of the component's series hold, and `offset` moves back from it by whole periods at the frame's grain, 0 for the anchor itself. It is resolved to a period label each time the component is drawn.
relative_period.$comment: dfo_frame_grammar.rolling resolves it: latest_anchor finds the anchor and shift_period applies the offset. A day-grain frame admits offset 0 only, and a span frame admits no relative period. `integer` admits an integral float such as -1.0, and shift_period takes an int, so a consumer converts the offset before calling.

window.description: Each side is a period label at the frame's grain, e.g. "2024", the frame's span, e.g. "2018/2022", or a relative period, e.g. {"anchor": "latest", "offset": -9}. An omitted side runs to the edge of the frame's coverage; omitting the window entirely means full coverage.
window.$comment: A label's maxLength is 21, the longest period the frame grammar's parse_time_period accepts: a day-grain span such as 2024-01-01/2024-01-31. The component schemas' $defs.observed_period carries the same bound.

stat_card.description: One value with its label and unit: the latest observed period within the window.

select.description: Dimension name to value, naming exactly one series.

change.description: A derived comparison between two observed periods of the primary series. `basis` names the two periods in order, from then to. `derivation` selects how the comparison is computed and absent means "difference".

basis.description: The two periods being compared, in order: [from, to]. Each is a period label or a relative period, e.g. [{"anchor": "latest", "offset": -1}, {"anchor": "latest", "offset": 0}].

derivation.description: How the change is computed. Absent means "difference".
